The Global Stroke Burden

Stroke remains the world’s leading cause of long-term adult disability — and upper-limb motor recovery is one of the largest unmet rehabilitation needs.

Patterns of Motor Paralysis
Monoplegia
Hemiplegia
Diplegia
Paraplegia
Quadriplegia
VRMT targets hemiplegia — one-sided motor loss seen in ~80% of stroke survivors at onset; ~50% remain impaired at 6 months.
Burden
12.2M new strokes / year · 101M survivors worldwide · US$891B annual cost (≈1.1% world GDP). Scalable, evidence-based upper-limb rehabilitation is a global priority.

Feigin VL et al. WSO Global Stroke Fact Sheet. Int J Stroke 2022;17:18–29  ·  Lawrence ES et al. Stroke 2001;32:1279–1284  ·  Kwakkel G et al. Stroke 2003;34:2181–2186.

穿戴科技與行動照護實驗室Wearable Technology and Mobile Healthcare Laboratory 5

Stroke HemiplegiaUnaffected vs Affected Side

Stroke causes one-sided motor loss — the patient retains an intact unaffected (健側) side and an impaired affected (患側) side. Mirror therapy is built to exploit this asymmetry.

Unaffected Side · 健側

Intact motor control

  • Full voluntary movement · preserved sensation & proprioception.
  • Serves as the visual driver in the mirror loop.
  • Provides the kinematic template for the cortex to re-learn.
Affected Side · 患側

Paretic / Paralysed limb

  • Weak or absent voluntary movement · spasticity, flexion synergy.
  • Impaired sensation & proprioceptive feedback.
  • The rehabilitation target — what mirror therapy aims to recover.
Target
Population
Unilateral chronic stroke patients with upper-limb hemiparesis · method: hand rehabilitation. Mirror therapy uses the unaffected side’s motion to drive cortical re-organisation of the affected side.

Lawrence ES et al. Stroke 2001;32:1279–1284  ·  Langhorne P et al. Lancet 2011;377:1693–1702  ·  Kwakkel G et al. Stroke 2003;34:2181–2186.

穿戴科技與行動照護實驗室Wearable Technology and Mobile Healthcare Laboratory 6

Traditional Mirror Therapy (MT)

A rehabilitation method using a mirror to project the unaffected limb’s motion onto the affected side — driving multisensory neuroplastic recovery.

Origin & Mechanism
  • Ramachandran & Rogers-Ramachandran (1996) — mirror visual feedback first used for phantom-limb pain.
  • Altschuler et al. (1999) — first application to stroke hemiparesis; brain perceives bilateral movement via the reflection.
Why It Works — Neural Mechanism
  • Multisensory integration — visual feedback substitutes for absent proprioception from the affected limb.
  • Bilateral cortical priming — mirror feedback rebalances motor-cortex activity between hemispheres.
  • Cochrane 2018 — moderate-quality evidence for upper-limb motor recovery (62 RCTs, ~1,982 patients).
CLASSICAL MIRROR-BOX SETUP

Ramachandran & Rogers-Ramachandran. Proc R Soc B 1996;263:377–386  ·  Altschuler EL et al. Lancet 1999;353:2035–2036  ·  Thieme H et al. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2018;7:CD008449.

穿戴科技與行動照護實驗室Wearable Technology and Mobile Healthcare Laboratory 7

Traditional Mirror Therapy (MT)Clinical Advantages — What the Evidence Shows

Across 60+ RCTs and recent 2025 meta-analyses (n > 600), classical mirror therapy delivers moderate, reproducible gains in four clinically meaningful domains.

Reduces upper-limb pain

Mirror visual feedback decreases neuropathic and post-stroke shoulder/hand pain via re-mapped sensorimotor representation.

Thieme Cochrane 2018 (n≈1,982) · Carrasco-Uribarren Healthcare 2024.

Improves hand & grip function

Task-based mirror therapy yields measurable gains in Fugl-Meyer hand subscale, grip strength, and dexterity.

Saragih Clin Rehabil 2025 (n=633, hand MD 1.48) · Arya Neurorehabil Neural Repair 2015.

Reduces inter-hemispheric asymmetry

Bilateral cortical priming rebalances motor-cortex activity, reducing pathological inter-hemispheric inhibition.

Hsieh PM&R 2025 (subacute meta) · Rossiter Neurorehabil Neural Repair 2015.

Improves ADL functionality

Gains transfer to activities of daily living — eating, dressing, grooming — the outcomes patients care about most.

Hsieh PM&R 2025 (ADL SMD 0.461) · Thieme Cochrane 2018.
Evidence
Strength
Moderate-quality evidence for upper-limb motor recovery; small but consistent effect sizes across 2018–2025 reviews. Mirror therapy is established — the open question is how to deliver it better.

Traditional Mirror Therapy (MT)Limitations — The Case for Immersive VR

The classical mirror-box constrains what can be trained, where it can be trained, and how sessions are dosed — gaps that an immersive VR delivery directly addresses.

Limitation 1

Unable for major-action rehabilitation

The mirror box reflects only a single sagittal-plane image of simple hand poses — no shoulder, no compound multi-joint reaching.

Futuretech 2020 · Thieme Cochrane 2018.
Limitation 2

High environmental distraction

Open-room setup; visual and auditory noise repeatedly breaks the illusion of bilateral movement the therapy depends on.

Yıldırım, Ağrı — J Turkish Soc Algology 2016.
Limitation 3

Restricted to simple, ungraded activities

No task variety, no progression, no objective dose tracking — the therapist must time and grade sessions manually.

therapydna314 2020 · Thieme Cochrane 2018.
Immersive VR Fix

Full 3-D scene, complex tasks

Stereoscopic depth + ego-centric viewpoint support compound multi-joint reaching, grasping, and bimanual coordination.

Immersive VR Fix

HMD blocks the room

Head-mounted display isolates the patient from environmental noise — sustained embodiment of the affected limb.

Immersive VR Fix

Gamified tasks, auto-dose tracking

Built-in hand tracking logs joint kinematics per session; gamified tasks scale difficulty automatically.

Why
VRMT
Preserve the neuroplastic mechanism. Fix the delivery. Keep the multisensory + bilateral-priming engine that makes MT work — remove the box, the noise, and the dosing gap with an immersive 3-D VR system.
穿戴科技與行動照護實驗室Wearable Technology and Mobile Healthcare Laboratory 9

VRMT — Virtual Reality Mirror Therapy

VRMT extends classical mirror therapy into an immersive 3-D scene — with real-time hand tracking and objective kinematic data.

VRMT IN PRACTICE
Key Differences from Classical MT

Built on classical MT, freed from the box

Keeps the multisensory neuroplastic engine of MT — replaces the bulky 2-D mirror with an immersive 3-D scene, real-time hand capture, and automatic kinematic logging.

  • Static 2-D reflection → immersive 3-D scene with stereoscopic depth.
  • Passive mirror → real-time motion capture of the unaffected hand.
  • No dose tracking → kinematic data captured per session.
  • Engaging, gamifiable — deployable at clinic and home.

Lin et al. IEEE Access 2021;9:14725–14734  ·  Hsu H-Y, Kuo L-C, Lin C-W, Su F-C, Yang T-H, Lin C-W. Neurorehabil Neural Repair 2022;36(6):335–345.

Virtual Reality Mirror Therapy (VRMT) from NCKUClinical Use & Patient Profile

⚕Clinical Indications

Who benefits clinically?

  • Patients with unilateral cerebral infarction or hemorrhage who have mild to severe motor impairments in the proximal and distal upper limbs.
  • Patients with hemiparesis who do not have significant cognitive or perceptual impairments.
Targets functional recovery of the affected upper limb in adult stroke rehabilitation.
♿Patient Types
  • Includes stroke and cerebral palsy patients.
🩺Clinical Users
  • Occupational therapists (OTs) and physical therapists (PTs).
  • Mirror therapy can be arranged by OTs/PTs in clinical rehabilitation settings.

What VRMT Does

An immersive virtual-reality alternative to the classical mirror box — the unaffected hand is captured, mirrored, and rendered as the affected hand in a real-time 3-D scene, driving motor recovery for upper-limb hemiparesis after stroke.

it works

Hand Motion CaptureThree Generations of VRMT Input

Capturing the unaffected hand drives the entire VRMT pipeline. Across three hardware generations the NCKU program has traded dedicated accuracy → zero hardware → integrated immersion — each iteration shrinking the setup burden.

Generation 1First VRMT prototype

Leap Motion Controller

Desk-mounted infrared optical sensor — 2 IR cameras + 3 LEDs reconstruct hand structure via stereo vision.

0.01 mm precision · 200 fps · 2 hands × 10 fingers
  • High kinematic fidelity — dedicated tracking volume.
  • Constrained interaction box; requires desk setup.
Lin et al. IEEE Access 2021;9:14725 · Hsu, Kuo, Lin et al. Neurorehabil Neural Repair 2022;36(6):335 · Cho et al. Med Sci Monit 2018.
Generation 2Markerless · low cost

Webcam + MediaPipe

Off-the-shelf RGB webcam feeding Google MediaPipe Hands — a deep-learning hand-landmark model.

21 keypoints/hand · 30 fps · ~95% rehab-task accuracy
  • Zero dedicated hardware — runs on any laptop or home PC.
  • 2-D depth ambiguity; sensitive to lighting & viewing angle.
Camargos et al. J NeuroEng Rehabil 2025 · Amprimo et al. Biomed Signal Process Control 2024 · Zhang et al. MediaPipe Hands, Google 2020.
Generation 3Current · production

Oculus / Meta Quest HMD

Quest 2/3 built-in 4× IR camera array + on-device CV pipeline — no external sensor, no controller.

24 hand joints · ego-centric viewpoint · stereoscopic 3-D scene
  • Tracking + immersive scene in one device — truly hands-free.
  • Dropout at extreme arm angles; HMD comfort for long sessions.
Abdlkarim et al. Sci Rep 2025 (Quest 2 validation) · Iruthayarajah et al. Sci Rep 2023 (low-cost VR MT) · Meta Hand Tracking SDK 2023.
穿戴科技與行動照護實驗室Wearable Technology and Mobile Healthcare Laboratory 15

MirroringSagittal-Plane Reflection of the Unaffected Hand

The system reflects the captured unaffected-hand pose across the user’s midline (sagittal plane), then renders it as the affected hand in an ego-centric scene — sustaining the multisensory illusion that re-engages the lesioned motor cortex.

Why It Works · Neural Rationale

Mirror Visual Feedback (MVF)

Congruent visual + proprioceptive input creates the illusion that the paretic limb is moving normally — bypassing learned non-use and re-engaging the lesioned hemisphere.

  • Stimulates the lesioned primary motor cortex (M1), premotor cortex, and parietal lobe.
  • Reduces pathological inter-hemispheric inhibition imbalance.
  • Drives activity-dependent neuroplasticity in the affected sensorimotor network.
Ramachandran & Rogers-Ramachandran Proc R Soc B 1996 · Thieme Cochrane 2018 · Rossiter Neurorehabil Neural Repair 2015.
How We Built It · NCKU Implementation

Meta Quest 2 + Oculus Interaction SDK

24 hand landmarks are tracked in real time without a controller. An OVRCustomHandPrefab renders the mirrored affected hand inside the user’s ego-centric VR scene.

  • Visual deception design — the mirrored hand is rendered in a realistic skin tone to maximise sense of ownership; the healthy hand is rendered in monotone gray to suppress visual interference.
  • VRMT-FOA extension — real-time eye-tracking + dual-task (arithmetic / card-sort) locks attention on the paretic workspace and boosts motor-cortex ERD.
Lin et al. IEEE Access 2021;9:14725 · Hsu, Kuo, Lin et al. Neurorehabil Neural Repair 2022;36(6):335.
Position Transform
MirrorPos = (−Px, Py, Pz)
Flip the X-coordinate across the sagittal plane; keep Y and Z.
Rotation Transform
MirrorRot = (Rx+180°, −Ry, Rz)
Symmetric Euler-angle transform on the three rotation axes.
Render Engine
Quaternion.Euler(…)
Unity converts Euler angles to quaternion before driving the 3-D hand model.
穿戴科技與行動照護實驗室Wearable Technology and Mobile Healthcare Laboratory 16

RenderingUnity-Based VRMT Family

Each Unity-based system renders the mirrored hand into a distinct virtual scene tuned to its therapeutic goal. The pipeline math is shared (see s12) — only the scene assets and hand-model fidelity differ. (SM-ARMT’s mobile AR stack → next slide.)

TO-VRMT

Oculus Rift + Unity

Unity + C# · Oculus Rift @ 90 Hz

Basic stick-and-ball skeleton hands; ADL objects rendered on a virtual table for task-oriented manipulation.

  • Hand model: white rods + blue joint balls.
  • Scene: pens, playing cards, coins + containers.
  • Mirror plane: X-axis inversion along Y-axis.
Fauzan & Lin Master’s Thesis, NCKU 2020.
MD-VRMT

Quest 2 + XR Toolkit

Unity + XR Interaction Toolkit · Quest 2

Audio-driven scene — a Mirror Drum with falling rhythm blocks; assets modeled in Blender, exported to Unity.

  • Scene: Mirror Drum + falling rhythm blocks + drumsticks.
  • Pipeline: Blender → Unity export.
  • Dynamic visual score feedback per drum hit.
Chen Y-W, Hsu H-Y, Lin C-W. WTMH Lab Poster.
RH-VRMT

Quest 2 + Oculus SDK 50

Unity 2021.3.8f1 · Oculus Interaction SDK 50.0

OVRCustomHandPrefab in a virtual living-room scene; visual deception via skin-tone asymmetry.

  • Hand: SyntheticHand smoothing + HandVisual mesh; dynamic palm scaling.
  • Color: affected = realistic skin, healthy = monotone gray.
  • No virtual robot in VR — TIGER acts physically via Arduino.
Liu & Lin Master’s Thesis, NCKU 2024.
Shared / Unity
Family Pipeline
TO · MD · RH all use the same C# transform script before mesh rendering: MirrorPos = (−Pḵ, Pḷ, PḺ) + Quaternion.Euler(Rḵ+180°, −Rḷ, RḺ) — only the scene assets and hand-model fidelity differ across systems.
穿戴科技與行動照護實驗室Wearable Technology and Mobile Healthcare Laboratory 17

Rendering · Mobile ARInside the iOS-Native Pipeline

SM-ARMT departs from Unity entirely. The pipeline runs natively on iOS, extracts the user’s hand as a 2-D contour, and overlays it onto the real-world camera feed — no 3-D mesh, no HMD, no PC.

Architecture

SwiftUI + Metal + ARKit 3

A custom iOS app processes the rear-camera stream entirely on-device. Different stack for a different use case — no Unity, no Oculus SDK.

  • SwiftUI — declarative UI shell for the iOS app.
  • Metal — Apple’s GPU API powers the overlay shader + Cardboard barrel-distortion.
  • ARHeadsetKit — Swift package for Cardboard dual-view rendering.
  • ARKit 3 Person Segmentation API — system-level human segmentation (replaces a custom U-Net prototype for ~3× speedup).
Visual Design

2-D Hand Contour, No 3-D Mesh

Instead of rendering a 3-D hand model, the system extracts the unaffected hand as a 2-D contour and pastes it — mirrored — directly onto the real-world camera background.

  • Motion-only mirroring — hand pixels only; no body, no virtual environment.
  • Avoids the uncanny valley of full-body 3-D rendering.
  • Cardboard support — dual-view + barrel distortion for stereoscopic parallax.
  • Patient’s own real-world background = familiar, low-distraction context.
Performance
& Pipeline
60 FPS overlay at 10–20 ms inference · iPhone 11+ (iOS 15+ / A12 Bionic+) · zero PC/HMD — most accessible family delivery.

ML PivotCustom U-Net + MobileNetV2 (dice 0.124, 35–40 ms, 25–28 FPS) → ARKit 3 Person Segmentation (10–20 ms, 60 FPS) · Cardboard via Metal shader · CPU:GPU 2:8 + shared frame buffer

Huang P-Y & Lin C-W. Development of iOS-based Augmented Reality Mirror Therapy Software for Upper Limb Rehabilitation in Stroke-Induced Hemiparesis. Master’s Thesis, National Cheng Kung University, 2023.

SM-VRMT — Simple Virtual Reality Mirror TherapyBaseline · Visual Feedback Only

The foundational system — replaces the classical mirror box with a fully immersive 3-D VR scene. No extra feedback modality beyond visual MVF.

Hardware & Method Meta Quest 2 + Leap Motion (sub-mm, 200 fps). Visual MVF only — no audio, haptic, or robotic assistance.
Pilot Results Stroke patients showed significant gains in FMA-UE + BBT (p < .05); SM-VRMT > traditional MT.

Lin C-W et al. IEEE Access 2021;9:14725 · Hsu, Kuo, Lin et al. Neurorehabil Neural Repair 2022;36(6):335.

穿戴科技與行動照護實驗室Wearable Technology and Mobile Healthcare Laboratory 21

TO-VRMT — Task-Oriented Mirror Therapy+ Task-Oriented Sensorimotor Feedback

Replaces simple repetitive joint movements with functional daily-life tasks — pen-grasping, card-flipping, coin placement — to combat boredom and sustain visual attention.

Hardware & Method

Oculus Rift + Leap Motion

Functional task scenarios are placed in the affected-limb workspace; patients perform ADL-like manipulations while receiving mirror visual feedback.

  • Headset: Oculus Rift.
  • Hand tracking: Leap Motion controller.
  • Feedback: visual MVF + task-oriented sensorimotor cues from interacting with virtual objects.
Study Design & Outcomes

2-Arm Pilot RCT · Healthy Young Adults

Short-term efficacy trial vs traditional task-oriented mirror box, with 2-hour follow-up.

  • Cohort: n=9 VRMT vs n=9 Trad MT (age ~22 yr).
  • Protocol: 30-min single session; assessed at T0 · post · 2-h follow-up.
  • Comparator: traditional task-oriented mirror box.
  • Outcomes: PHUA, MMDT (turning + placing), PPT (assembly), SWM, Grasp Power.
Pilot
Results
+ MMDT Turning — the only between-group significant outcome: VRMT 80.8 → 66.6 s vs Trad 86.0 → 71.6 s (F=5.289, p=.036, η²=.261).
± Within-group sig: PHUA FP/FRpeak (p≤.002) · MMDT both subtests (VRMT). − n.s.: PPT Assembly trend (p=.06), SWM, Grasp Power.

ML PipelineLeap Motion 100 Hz + 4 Hz low-pass (order 3) + LSTM trajectory prediction · X-axis RMSE 0.0337

Fauzan L & Lin C-W. Development of a Virtual Reality Rehabilitation System based on Task-Oriented Mirror Therapy and its Verification on Healthy Subjects. Master’s Thesis, National Cheng Kung University, 2020.

穿戴科技與行動照護實驗室Wearable Technology and Mobile Healthcare Laboratory 22

MD-VRMT — Music-Driven Mirror Therapy+ Rhythmic Audio + Vibration Feedback

Adds synchronous rhythmic music and controller vibration to the visual mirror illusion — a tri-modal feedback loop (visual + audio + haptic) on a Mirror-Drum interface.

Hardware & Method

Quest 2 + Controllers + OpenBCI

Synchronous music plays as the patient strikes a virtual “Mirror Drum”; VR controllers provide haptic vibration; EEG monitors cortical activation.

  • Headset: Meta Quest 2.
  • Peripherals: VR Controllers (haptic vibration) + OpenBCI Cyton EEG cap.
  • Feedback: visual + audio + haptic.
Study Design & Outcomes

Stroke Parallel RCT + Healthy Crossover

Two distinct study designs — clinical efficacy on stroke + mechanism probing on healthy.

  • Stroke: n=20 chronic hemiplegic, 2-arm parallel 1:1 (Mirror Drum vs traditional MT; usual care given to both).
  • Stroke dose: 50 min therapy + 20 min usual care, 2 days/wk × 9 weeks.
  • Healthy: n=60, 3-condition crossover 1:1:1 — Mirror Drum w/ music · w/o music · MT (10 min EEG + 10 min therapy, 1-wk washout).
  • Outcomes: stroke — FMA-UE, MAS, BBT, SWM, MAL, CGI; healthy — PHUA + EEG ERD/Coherence.
Pilot
Results
Stroke: FMA-UE total p=.007, shoulder p=.001 vs MT. Healthy EEG: music+vibration ↑ Mu/Beta ERD — qualitative only.

MD PipelineDemucs source-separation · OpenBCI Cyton 1–50 Hz · pwelch() PSD + mscohere() coherence
Caveats: n=20 stroke · only shoulder p=.001 · no effect sizes/CIs · healthy EEG qualitative only

Chen Y-W, Hsu H-Y, Lin C-W. Rhythmic Music + Vibration Stimulation for VRMT. WTMH Lab Poster.

穿戴科技與行動照護實驗室Wearable Technology and Mobile Healthcare Laboratory 23

RH-VRMT — Robotic-Hand Mirror Therapy+ Active Mechanical Movement (Proprioceptive)

Adds active mechanical movement of the affected hand via a wrist exoskeleton + soft glove — visual MVF gains a proprioceptive partner.

Hardware & Method

Quest 2 + TIGER Exoskeleton + Soft Glove

Two operating modes: synchronous — the healthy hand drives the robotic device on the affected hand; passive — the robot drives the affected hand independently.

  • Headset: Meta Quest 2 + Leap Motion.
  • Robotics: Arduino Uno + TIGER wrist exoskeleton + soft ROBOT glove.
  • EEG: OpenBCI Cyton for cortical activation + coherence.
Study Design & Outcomes

5-Condition Crossover vs Pure VRMT

2 robots (TIGER + soft ROBOT) × 2 modes (synchronous / passive) + baseline.

  • Cohort: n=30 right-handed healthy young adults.
  • Conditions: VRMT · Syn + soft ROBOT · Alt + passive soft · Syn + TIGER · Alt + passive TIGER.
  • Protocol: 5 × 20-min sessions, 1-week washouts; randomized order.
  • Outcomes: PHUA, PPT, MMDT, 2PD, SWM + EEG ERD/ERS · Coherence.
Pilot
Results
Syn VRMT + TIGER vs VRMT: significantly stronger Beta ERD in right-lateralized frontal areas — right prefrontal p=.019, frontal p=.03, right frontal p=.012. Frontal-occipital coherence also gains (F3–O2 p=.036, F7–O2 p=.037) — objective evidence the robotic add-on engages broader cortical networks.

Caveatshealthy n=30 ceiling effect · OpenBCI Cyton+Daisy (consumer-grade EEG, not medical) · pneumatic-pump latency limits real-time sync · rest-vs-movement eye-closure confounds ERD attribution

Liu T-H & Lin C-W. Hybrid System for Robot-Assisted VR Mirror Therapy Targeting Distal Joints of the Upper Limb. NCKU master’s thesis, 2024.

SM-ARMT — Simple Augmented Reality Mirror TherapyiOS-Based · Mobile Telerehabilitation

Drops the VR headset entirely — a smartphone’s rear camera + ML body-segmentation network mirrors the hand onto a real-world background for accessible at-home telerehab. Equipment economy: VR-MT stack $1k–15k → smartphone $300–800 + Cardboard $3–20.

Hardware & Method

iPhone (iOS) + Cardboard

A custom iOS app processes the rear-camera stream through a human-body semantic-segmentation neural net at 60 fps; only the hand motion is mirrored, avoiding the uncanny-valley effect of full-body rendering.

  • Device: iOS smartphone (iPhone 11 tested) + optional Cardboard headset for 3-D split-screen view.
  • Method: motion-only mirroring on real-world background.
  • No expensive VR/PC setup — pure mobile.
Study Design & Findings

Crossover RCT vs Traditional MT

Within-subject design with both behavioral and cortical-perfusion measurement.

  • Cohort: n=30 young healthy, 30-min ARMT + 30-min MT, 1-week washout.
  • Outcomes: PHUA, PPT, MMDT, 2PD, SWM + fNIRS prefrontal.
  • fNIRS: bilateral prefrontal synchrony ρ>0.9 in both arms; no group difference — equivalent neural signature.
  • Behavior: ARMT > MT on 9 of 12 outcomes (p<.05); see chart ↓
Δ from
Baseline

Mobile PipelineARKit 3 Person Segmentation · 10–20 ms → 60 FPS · iOS 15+ / A12 Bionic+ floor

Bars show Δ% from baseline; the −12% on PPT non-DH is the traditional-MT control arm regressing — mobile ARMT preserves while MT actively interferes on the dominant–non-dominant transfer task.  Huang P-Y & Lin C-W. iOS-based AR Mirror Therapy Software for Upper-Limb Rehabilitation in Stroke-Induced Hemiparesis. VRMT-FOA — Gaze-Guided Mirror TherapyFocused Objective Attention · Neural Evidence

In standard VRMT, patients drift into an autopilot state — eyes wander, sensory neglect returns. VRMT-FOA locks attention on the paretic workspace with a decide-then-act dual task, and verifies it with eye-tracking + EEG.

Gap in Regular VRMT

Autopilot & Sensory Neglect

Patients passively receive the mirror illusion; after a few minutes they perform repetitive motor tasks without active visual or cognitive engagement — rehab efficacy plateaus.

  • No objective measure of where the patient is looking.
  • Goal-directed attention is what drives synaptic modification & activity-dependent plasticity.
FOA Design

“Decide-then-Act” Dual Task

A cognitive challenge is presented in the affected-limb workspace; the patient must solve, then move — forcing sustained focus on the paretic side before and during execution.

  • Move Forward + Math · Pull Out + Color Matching · Circle + Reading
  • Put Coins + Color Matching · Shoot Ball + Counting · Flip Cards + Visual Matching
Hardware Delta

Quest Pro + OpenBCI Cyton

Step up from Quest 2 to Meta Quest Pro for built-in eye-tracking, paired with continuous EEG via OpenBCI Cyton.

  • Eye-tracking — real-time gaze trajectories on the patient’s view.
  • EEG — Mu (8–13 Hz) + Beta (13–30 Hz); thesis-explicit ROIs C3 / C4 motor cortex, plus prefrontal + parietal.
Pilot

Clinical Evidence · Stroke RCTsTwo of Six Systems Have Full Hemiplegia Trials

Of the six family systems, only SM-VRMT and MD-VRMT have full chronic-stroke RCTs. The other four (TO / RH / ARMT / VRMT-FOA) were validated on healthy adults first — stroke validation is the next translational step.

SM-VRMT · Baseline

Three-Arm RCT, 9–12 Weeks

First validation of digital MVF — immersive VR replaces the physical mirror box for chronic-stroke hemiplegia patients.

  • Population: n=54 chronic stroke hemiplegia.
  • Design: 3-arm RCT — VRMT vs conventional MT vs conventional OT.
  • Outcomes: FMA-UE, Box and Block Test.
  • Result: Significant gains in wrist motion + coordination; FMA-UE change exceeds controls.
MD-VRMT · Multisensory

Multisensory Stroke RCT

9-week multisensory intervention — Mirror Drum + synchronous music + vibration vs traditional MT (both arms also receive usual care).

  • Population: n=20 chronic hemiplegic stroke.
  • Design: 2-arm parallel RCT, 50 min therapy + 20 min usual care, 2 days/wk × 9 weeks.
  • Outcomes: FMA-UE, MAS, BBT, SWM, MAL, CGI.
  • Result: FMA-UE total p=.007; shoulder subscale p=.001 (elbow/forearm not reported).
Evidence
Gaps
Drop-out, blinding, long-term follow-up not reported across the family. CI / Cohen’s d not provided — only p-values and percentage changes. Stroke RCTs for TO / RH / ARMT / VRMT-FOA remain pending translation work.

Lin C-W et al. IEEE Access 2021;9:14725 · Hsu, Kuo, Lin et al. Neurorehabil Neural Repair 2022;36(6):335 · Chen Y-W, Hsu H-Y, Lin C-W. WTMH Lab Poster.

Citation ReceptionHsu 2022 NNR in subsequent systematic reviews

Hsu, Kuo, Lin et al. NNR 2022 — the 3-arm RCT (n=54, MT / COT / VR-MT) anchoring SM-VRMT — has been re-analyzed in 5+ systematic reviews (2023–2025). The pooled verdict: consistently positive, methodologically “moderate quality.”

Included In · 5 Recent Reviews

2023–2025 Systematic Reviews + Meta-Analyses

  • Tian et al. 2023 · Front Neurol — VR-MT specific meta (most direct).
  • JMIR 2025 e73142 — Combined immersive + non-immersive VR + MT.
  • Saragih et al. 2025 · Clin Rehabil — 18 RCTs, n=633 stroke.
  • Hsieh et al. 2025 · PM&R — subacute MT meta-analysis.
  • Hao 2024 · Health Sci Rep — VR stroke rehab umbrella review.
Pooled Effect Sizes

Direction: significant + positive

Across meta-analyses including Hsu 2022, VR-MT outperforms traditional MT on motor + dexterity outcomes.

  • Tian 2023: FMA-UE SMD 0.81 (large) · BBT SMD 0.48 · MFT SMD 0.72.
  • JMIR 2025: FMA-UE MD 3.50 (95% CI 1.47–5.53; p=.0007) · BBT MD 1.09 (p=.03).
  • Hsu’s own: FMA-UE +3.8 (9wk) / +4.2 (12wk) · BBT +2.9 / +3.1 · hand subscale p=.01 vs MT.
Strengths
vs Limits
+ Strengths: rare 3-arm design (MT · COT · VR-MT), 12-wk follow-up, sig. hand-subscale gain, consistently positive across reviews.
− Limits: small n=54, no VR blinding, pooled FMA-UE below MCID, no long-term follow-up.

Tian Front Neurol 2023 · JMIR 2025;27:e73142 · Saragih Clin Rehabil 2025 · Hsieh PM&R 2025 · Hao Health Sci Rep 2024. (Original: Hsu et al. NNR 2022;36(6):335.)

Objective BiomarkersEEG · fNIRS · Gaze Tracking Across the Family

Beyond clinical scales, the program quantifies mirror-therapy mechanisms with cortical (EEG), hemodynamic (fNIRS), and oculomotor (gaze) biomarkers — objective evidence for how the therapy works.

MD-VRMT — Multisensory EEG

n=60 healthy 3-condition crossover (Mirror Drum w/ music · w/o music · MT). Adding music + vibration visibly increased Mu / Beta ERD in the motor cortex — qualitative observation; poster does not report exact p-values.

Marker: EEG ERD & Coherence · Chen Y-W, Hsu H-Y, Lin C-W. WTMH Poster.

RH-VRMT — Robot + EEG Coherence

Healthy crossover (5 conditions). Syn VRMT + TIGER vs VRMT: stronger Beta ERD in right-lateralized frontal areas (right prefrontal p=.019 · frontal p=.03 · right frontal p=.012); frontal–occipital coherence gains (F3–O2 p=.036, F7–O2 p=.037).

Marker: EEG Beta ERD + Frontal–Occipital Coherence · Liu & Lin 2024.

SM-ARMT — fNIRS Hemodynamics

n=30 healthy crossover. Prefrontal bilateral synchrony equally strong in both arms (ARMT ρ=.961 · MT ρ=.969). Motor cortex bilateral synchrony notably lower in ARMT than MT (ρ=.344 vs .782) — mobile AR engages frontal attention well but recruits less bilateral motor cooperation. ARMT still wins behaviorally on 9 of 12 clinical outcomes (slide 34).

Marker: fNIRS prefrontal perfusion · Huang & Lin 2023.

VRMT-FOA — Gaze + Strongest ERD

Affected-side gaze ratio 36% → 64% → 71% (VRMT → VRMT-FOA → +Audio); gaze-duration +77% / +98%. Strongest, most stable Mu / Beta ERD across motor, prefrontal, parietal cortices; VRMT-FOA-AF also showed the most persistent inter-regional coherence (qualitative).

Marker: Eye-tracking + EEG ERD/Coherence · Huang A-T, Hsu H-Y, Lin C-W.

Cortical Network EngagementRH-VRMT EEG Coherence · Robot Augments Inter-Regional Connectivity

Robot-augmented conditions enhance EEG coherence not only during active hand movement, but also at rest — suggesting neural carryover beyond active engagement. Strongest single effect: Fz–O1 Mu p<.001 (rest phase, Syn TIGER vs Alt TIGER).

Representative Pairs
Hand-movement phase · robot vs pure VRMT
Mu band (8–12 Hz)
Beta band (13–30 Hz)
9 findings · 30+ sig pairs across 4 robot conditions vs VRMT

Phase-Specific Themes
  • Movement: motor → occipital/parietal (Mu) + bilateral frontal recruitment (Beta) + central-vertical axis (Mu).
  • Rest: right-hemisphere vertical Fz–O1 p<.001 dominates; left central-frontal (Beta) sustained; occipital suppression also present.
  • Interpretation: connectivity does not collapse at rest — robot effect carries over, suggesting neural plasticity beyond task period.

Bilateral Hemispheric SynchronySM-ARMT fNIRS · ARMT vs Traditional MT · Prefrontal Symmetric, Motor Asymmetric

In healthy subjects, prefrontal L–R synchrony stays high in both arms; but motor-cortex bilateral synchrony drops sharply in ARMT — mobile AR engages frontal attention without recruiting equivalent bilateral motor cooperation. Behavioral superiority persists (slide 34).

Bilateral L–R Synchrony (ρ)
Pearson correlation between L & R hemispheric HbO — per region
ρ > 0.7: strong bilateral coupling
ρ < 0.5: weak / asymmetric (dashed)
NIRScout: 16 detectors + 8 sources · 3 cm spacing
Tracked over prefrontal cortex + motor cortex (4 regional quadrants)
Key Findings
  • Prefrontal bilateral synchrony stays robust (ρ ≈ .97) regardless of condition — frontal attention recruited equally.
  • Motor cortex bilateral synchrony drops to ρ=.344 in ARMT vs .782 in MT — mobile AR fails to engage bilateral motor cooperation.
  • GLM activation: no significant group difference in any region (all p>.05) — "similar excitation patterns" per author. Asymmetry shows in connectivity, not activation magnitude.

Huang P-Y & Lin C-W. iOS-based AR Mirror Therapy. NCKU master’s thesis, 2023 (Table 8.2 GLM p-values; Figure 23 fNIRS layout). Behavioral comparison see slide 25 + slide 34.

AR Direction · From Phone to FutureMirror Therapy Beyond the Headset

AR democratizes the program — unlimited home training for less than one PT session; no $1–15K headset, no pre-set safety zone, real-world context preserved. The lab’s AR thrust runs on consumer iPhones — no AR-glasses pivot planned.

Why AR Motivation

Accessibility + Ownership

VR costs $1–15K + needs a safety zone — clinic-only. Consumer AR runs on phones patients already own.

  • Unlimited home training for less than one PT session.
  • Own skin + lighting — higher ownership than a generic VR avatar.
  • Avoids 2-D-flip uncanny valley (moles / scars on wrong side).

Why Edge-AI for the Heart?The Screening & AI Gap

Arrhythmias are intermittent — easy to miss in a short clinic ECG — yet most cleared devices still carry no AI at all.

⚠The screening gap

Caught only if it happens to fire

  • Atrial fibrillation and ectopic beats are paroxysmal — a 10-second clinic ECG often misses them.
  • Definitive 12-lead diagnosis stays hospital-bound — it needs a clinic and a cardiologist to read.
Screening has to move to where the patient already is.
▲The AI gap
  • Only 8 of 204 FDA 510(k) devices (Jan–Jul 2022) shipped AI/ML — 96% have none.
  • 4 of 52 ECG monitors (Jan–Sep 2024) — the cardiology gap persists.
●The opening
  • Lightweight AI small enough to run on the device itself — no cloud, no GPU.
  • The wearable PAG sensor is already IEC 60601-1 safety-certified.

Two Ways to Listen to the HeartPulse Audiogram · ECG

The lab works two complementary front-ends — a cuffless wearable sensor for everyday screening, and ECG for diagnostic confirmation.

♥Pulse Audiogram (PAG)

Piezoelectric radial-artery sensor

  • A cuffless, wearable piezoelectric sensor reads the radial-artery pulse waveform.
  • Detects atrial fibrillation and pulse-amplitude variation.
  • Passed IEC 60601-1 medical electrical-safety testing.
IEEE Access 2020 · HI-POCT 2017.
∿Standard ECG
  • Single-lead patch (ESP32-S3) for continuous wear; 12-lead for full diagnosis.
  • Gold-standard waveform for ectopic-beat and structural-heart-disease screening.
⇄Why use both
  • PAG = everyday screening; ECG = diagnostic confirmation — one shared lightweight-AI back-end.
穿戴科技與行動照護實驗室Wearable Technology and Mobile Healthcare Laboratory 39

Lightweight AI Model FamilyClassify · Detect · Learn from Less

The core idea — shrink CNN / YOLO models from hundreds of MB to hundreds of KB without losing accuracy.

▤Classify — lightweight CNNs
  • SEmbedNet — 3 conv + 2 FC layers, 56×56 input; 955× smaller than its baseline.
  • LMUEBCNet — reads CWT spectrograms; ~1 MB, only 10% of AlexNet's parameters.
  • 1D vs 2D — 1D models skip the heavy CWT step; LMUEBCNet-1D cuts inference 96% → 11 ms.
Scales from 5- to 9-class ectopic-beat typing.
⊞Detect — YOLO on ECG strips
  • ST-YOLO-LCv1 / YOLO-ResTinyECG — one-stage detectors that localise and classify beats on 5–20 s ECG.
  • Custom ResTinyECG backbone, pruned to just 0.1 M parameters.
≡Learn from scarce data
  • Siamese few-shot — learns rare arrhythmias from 1–5 samples/class (13.7 k params).
  • Corr-OS oversampling — balances MIT-BIH in ~100 s, keeps ECG morphology intact.

Does the AI See What a Cardiologist Sees?Explainable AI · Class Activation Mapping

Class Activation Mapping overlays prove the model focuses on real cardiac physiology — not artefacts.

♥CAM finds real physiology
  • For normal beats — CAM lights up the P wave, QRS complex and T wave.
  • For premature ventricular contractions — it highlights the wide QRS and the missing P wave.
Explainability is what earns clinical trust.
▤Why CAM over the rest
  • Guided Backprop — degenerates into generic edge detection.
  • Grad-CAM — sometimes misses the physiological feature entirely.
  • CAM — the clearest, most cardiologist-aligned explanation.
